problem: Open-vocabulary 3D semantic mapping systems (ConceptGraphs, HOV-SG) are slow and memory-heavy because of costly 3D inter-object merging and they assume static scenes. Dynamic-aware systems (OpenIN, Khronos) are offline, closed-set, or lack a strategy for finding relocated objects.
motivation: Robots in human environments need open-vocabulary queries, efficient online mapping, and robustness to objects that move. Keeping precise details of every object globally is unnecessary and fragile under change: stable structure suffices for high-level planning, and object details can be recovered by local online perception.
key_idea: Build a fast online concrete object map with a hybrid YOLO+FastSAM frontend and cheap intra-object checks, abstract it into a map of static anchor objects plus layout, and navigate by choosing candidates on the global abstract map and confirming the target on a locally built concrete map that updates the abstract map when the target has moved.
insight: Holistic 2D segmentation makes 3D inter-object merging unnecessary; the stability check alone brings ODR from 26.5 to 2.41 and cuts TPF from 2.841 to 0.3056 s, and dropping merging entirely gives 0.163 s TPF with ODR 2.56. For relocated objects, updating the abstract map during navigation lifts cross-anchor SR from 47.2% (original map) to 60.3%, versus 13.2% for random picking, so information gathered along the way matters. The weighted image+text feature matters too: w/o weighted feats mIoU drops from 0.2538 to 0.1814.
method: Hybrid segmentation frontend: YOLOv8l-world (class list from an LLM) plus MobileSAM masks, with overlapping boxes merged by RGB histogram similarity; FastSAM adds non-overlapping segments for classes outside the list, with YOLO taking priority.
Semantic feature embedding: object feature = 0.7*CLIP image feature + 0.3*CLIP text feature of the class label (mean text feature for 'null' FastSAM segments); MobileCLIP-S2 is used.

Concrete map update: observations are matched to objects by cosine similarity plus 3D overlap with threshold tau; matched objects are updated by weighted feature averaging and point cloud augmentation, otherwise a new object is created; there is no inter-object 3D merging.

Intra-object status checks: a stability check removes objects with too few observations or with a dominant class ID under 2/3; split detection separates under-segmented objects when different class IDs co-occur at the same timestamps.

Map abstraction: objects are classified as anchor (static) or volatile with CLIP similarity to example lists and phrase templates (margin 0.05, tau_a=0.5); volatile features are attached to the anchors they sit 'on'; a BEV occupancy layout is built from a scene point cloud.

Candidate retrieval and navigation: the query CLIP feature is scored against the anchor feature and its attached volatile features; a Voronoi global path leads to the best anchor and RRT* local planning goes to a confident match found in the local concrete map.

Online abstract-map update and re-selection: if no match is found near the anchor, the local concrete map is merged into the abstract map by overlap thresholds tau1/tau2 and the next-best anchor is chosen (up to 3 attempts).

setting.backbone: YOLOv8l-world + FastSAM-s + MobileSAM + MobileCLIP-S2 (all frozen, pretrained); GPT-4/4o used once to generate the class list
setting.observation: posed RGB-D frames (external pose; LiDAR FastLIO2 pose on real robots)
setting.action_space: planned paths (Voronoi global path plus RRT* local path) executed by the agent
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D scenes with YCB objects); Replica and ScanNet for mapping; real world
setting.privileged: GT camera poses (no pose estimation); GT object-level dynamics are only used to set up the test scenes

numbers_note: No standard benchmarks (R2R, ObjNav, etc.) are used. Navigation is evaluated on custom HM3D scenes with added YCB objects, and real-world SR is reported per scene (e.g. Meeting Room static 85.7%, dynamic 70.3%).
results: On Replica DualMap reaches mIoU 0.2538 versus 0.2050 for HOV-SG and 0.1501 for ConceptGraphs, cutting peak memory by more than 96% and TPF by 99.3% versus HOV-SG. Static HM3D navigation SR is 70.5% versus 61.5% for ConceptGraphs and 52.6% for HOV-SG. In dynamic scenes SR is 64.8% (in-anchor) and 60.3% (cross-anchor), and the real-world results are similar.
limitations: Relies on external pose estimation, since DualMap does not estimate camera pose itself.
No human-object interaction reasoning; the 'on' relation is the only spatial relation used.
Performance drops outdoors because of higher sensor noise, and dynamic-scene evaluation uses small self-built benchmarks with only two baselines and only in static settings.
